battle.name: 古巴革命
battle.brief: 古巴革命始於一九五三年，是推翻巴蒂斯塔統治並延續至一九五九年的武裝衝突，戰事遍及古巴各地。這場鬥爭的早期武器仍帶有十九世紀制式輕武器的特徵，雷管步槍（Percussion rifle）於一八四〇年列裝，反映交戰各方裝備世代並存。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管步槍屬於十九世紀步兵制式輕武器體系，作為前膛槍械用於一般射擊，並納入部隊標準配發與訓練。

countries: 交戰國與戰區：古巴是唯一直接發生武裝衝突的國家。1953年7月26日的主要戰鬥發生於聖地亞哥-德古巴東南的Moncada兵營；聖地亞哥的駐軍與營區管理單位負責防守，哈瓦那則是總統府、軍方最高指揮與革命組織活動的重要中心。支持Fulgencio Batista的政府軍由古巴陸軍、總統府警衛隊及後勤通信單位組成，26 de Julio運動則由Fidel Castro領導發動攻擊。美國當時在古巴有外交、貿易及軍方聯絡，但沒有直接投入1953年的戰鬥，因此是外部關係方而非戰役參戰國。本文依事件先後交代1952年底的政治動員、1953年的數次武裝行動、Moncada主戰鬥及其後果，並以1959年的政權更替標示全程終點。
countriesEn: Belligerent country and theater: Cuba was the only country in which armed conflict directly occurred. The principal engagement of July 26, 1953, took place at the Moncada barracks southeast of Santiago de Cuba. The Santiago garrison and the barracks administration were responsible for its defense, while Havana was the principal center for the presidency, the military high command, and revolutionary organization. The government forces supporting Fulgencio Batista consisted of the Cuban Army, the Presidential Guard, and logistical and communications units, while the 26th of July Movement directed the attack under Fidel Castro. The United States maintained diplomatic, commercial, and military contacts in Cuba but did not enter the fighting in 1953, making it an external interested party rather than a belligerent. This account follows the sequence of events from the political mobilization of late 1952, through the armed actions of 1953 and the battle at Moncada, to its aftermath, with the change of government in 1959 marking the end of the complete revolutionary sequence.
people: 主要人物與職責：Fidel Castro既是26 de Julio運動的政治領袖，也是Moncada主攻隊的指揮者；他在攻占初期控制局面，卻在撤退時被政府軍封鎖線截住。Raúl Castro負責武器取得、住宿點安排、交通與後勤，並與Fidel一同參與Moncada。José Antonio Echeverría主要維持政治組織、宣傳與聯絡，不應被寫成Moncada營區內的指揮者。Abel Santamaría與Juan Almeida Bosque指揮突擊、武器庫及廣播節點的分隊；營區方面的關鍵軍官是Antonio Varas。Fulgencio Batista是軍政核心，其政府決定增援、追擊與拘禁政策。Frank País在聖地亞哥建立地下組織，參與4月30日Goayería兵營襲擊，並於7月30日戰死。西班牙共和國軍人Alberto Bayo的游擊訓練思想影響過部分策劃者，但他不是1953年7月26日Moncada的直接指揮者。各人當日位置與分隊次序多靠回憶重建，若資料互相衝突，應保留可確認的指揮關係，不把推測寫成命令。
peopleEn: Principal figures and responsibilities: Fidel Castro was both the political leader of the 26th of July Movement and the commander of the main attacking force at Moncada. He controlled the early phase of the assault but was intercepted by a government roadblock while attempting to withdraw. Raúl Castro handled the acquisition of weapons, the arrangement of lodging, transport, and logistics, and participated in Moncada alongside Fidel. José Antonio Echeverría concentrated on political organization, propaganda, and liaison; he should not be represented as a commander inside the Moncada barracks. Abel Santamaría and Juan Almeida Bosque led detachments assigned to the assault, the armory, and broadcasting facilities. Antonio Varas was the significant military officer on the barracks side. Fulgencio Batista was the center of the military and political regime, and his government determined the policies for reinforcement, pursuit, and detention. Frank País built an underground organization in Santiago, participated in the April 30 attack on the Goayería barracks, and was killed in action on July 30. The guerrilla thinking of Spanish Republican officer Alberto Bayo influenced some of the planners, but he was not the direct commander of Moncada on July 26, 1953. Many details concerning individual positions and the sequence of the detachments were reconstructed from recollection; where accounts conflict, the verifiable chain of command should be retained rather than converting speculation into orders.
kits: 裝備並非制式化的單一系統。Moncada進攻者事前主要依靠手槍、步槍、少量自動武器和自備交通，進入兵營後才指望取得軍械庫。實際使用過或可確認在古巴軍方序列中的型號，包括西班牙製Mauser Model 1895及Model 1900栓動步槍、Remington Model 8半自動步槍、Thompson Model 1928衝鋒槍、Browning Automatic Rifle Model 1918，以及Colt Model 1903手槍與Browning M1935手槍。對應口徑包括7.65×54mmR、.30-06、.45 ACP、.32 ACP及9×19mm；同批武器的彈匣形式與備件並不完全互通。裝甲與機動方面，古巴軍方使用過GMC CCKW兩噸半六輪卡車、1947年後生產的雪佛蘭Advance Design卡車及Willys MB吉普，這些車輛可用於運人、運槍和轉運傷員，遠距離行動則主要依賴馬匹、騾子與徒步。通信使用商用短波收發機、軍用電話與蓄電池，後勤則包括水壺、口糧、繃帶、繩索、地圖與指南針。Moncada的核心問題不是完全沒有槍，而是可用彈藥不足、備援未能及時送達，車輛和道路也無法保證突擊隊安全帶走裝備。
kitsEn: The equipment was not standardized around a single system. Before the attack, the Moncada force depended mainly on pistols, rifles, a limited number of automatic weapons, and its own transport, expecting to obtain the army's armory only after entering the barracks. Models actually used or confirmed as part of Cuban military holdings included the Spanish Mauser Model 1895 and Model 1900 bolt-action rifles, the Remington Model 8 semiautomatic rifle, the Thompson Model 1928 submachine gun, the Browning Automatic Rifle Model 1918, the Colt Model 1903 pistol, and the Browning M1935 pistol. Their corresponding calibers included 7.65×54mmR, .30-06, .45 ACP, .32 ACP, and 9×19mm; magazines and spare parts within the same collection were not universally interchangeable. For transport, the Cuban military used the GMC CCKW 2.5-ton six-wheel truck, Chevrolet Advance Design trucks produced from 1947 onward, and the Willys MB jeep. These could carry personnel, weapons, and wounded, while long-distance movement otherwise depended on horses, mules, and travel on foot. Communications equipment included commercial shortwave transceivers, military telephones, and batteries. Logistics supplies consisted of canteens, rations, bandages, rope, maps, and compasses. The central problem at Moncada was not an absolute absence of weapons, but insufficient usable ammunition, failure to deliver the reserve promptly, and a lack of vehicles and secure routes for carrying equipment away.
tactics: 戰術經過：游擊隊先把人員分成主攻、封鎖外圍、交通與廣播等小組，黎明前由聖地亞哥東南方接近Moncada；正面小組製造混亂後，主隊進入營區，目標是奪取武器庫、彈藥與通信設備，而不是長期占領哈瓦那。哈瓦那方面另有人試圖襲擊Goayería兵營以牽制援軍，但未能切斷聖地亞哥方向的反擊。約清晨六時進攻後，進攻者一度控制主營區、武器庫和部分廣播設施，並向外發出簡短通告；然而兵營不是一座空殼，預定運來補充彈藥的車輛未能及時接上攻勢，守軍利用營區、鄰近據點與道路逐段反擊。午後政府增援抵達，進攻隊失去彈藥連續射擊與轉移空間，只能嘗試沿通往Sierra Maestra的道路突圍；Fidel與Raúl所率的一批人在山區封鎖線被截住，其餘各隊分散退出。4月30日的Goayería正面襲擊同樣未能帶走武器，而12月2日哈瓦那Banco Nacional de Cuba小組則採取短時間進入、廣播與迅速撤離的辦法。兩次結果顯示，死守固定市區據點而缺乏彈藥與退路，會使突擊隊被分割；以小隊游動、伏擊、破壞交通及保存力量的游擊方式，則成為下一階段方向。現有史料對個別突入點與分隊先後略有差異，但上述主幹並不靠猜測補足。
tacticsEn: Tactical course of action: The insurgents first divided into small teams for the main assault, isolation of the perimeter, transport, and broadcasting. Before dawn they approached Moncada from the highlands southeast of Santiago. After small groups created confusion at the front, the main body entered the barracks with the objective of taking the armory, ammunition, and communications equipment rather than permanently occupying Havana. A separate effort in Havana was made to attack the Goayería barracks and divert reinforcements, but it failed to prevent the response directed at Santiago. At approximately six in the morning, the attackers briefly took control of the main section of the barracks, the armory, and part of the broadcasting equipment, and issued a short communiqué. The barracks, however, was not empty. The vehicles intended to bring a replenishment of ammunition did not connect with the attack in time, and the defenders used the barracks, neighboring posts, and roads to counterattack section by section. Government reinforcements arrived during the afternoon, depriving the attackers of both ammunition for sustained fire and room to maneuver. They attempted to break out along the road toward Sierra Maestra, but Fidel, Raúl, and a portion of their group were stopped at a mountain roadblock while the other detachments dispersed. The frontal attack on Goayería on April 30 likewise failed to carry away weapons, whereas the small Banco Nacional de Cuba team in Havana on December 2 used a brief entry, a broadcast, and a rapid withdrawal. These contrasting results showed that holding a fixed urban position without ammunition and an exit route fragmented the assault force. Mobile teams conducting ambushes, disrupting transport, and preserving strength became the next strategic direction. Sources differ slightly over individual entry points and the sequence of detachments, but this established outline does not depend on filling gaps by guesswork.
data: 時間與可核對的節點如下：1952年12月2日，Fidel在哈瓦那Palacio de Deportes發表推翻現政府的公開演說；1953年4月30日，革命網絡襲擊哈瓦那Goayería兵營，武器未能奪取，攻擊者遭受重創；7月26日，逾百名武裝及接應者在黎明前集結，約六時對Moncada發動攻擊，上午短暫控制兵營，午後因增援與彈藥不足而崩解，Fidel、Raúl等人被俘或受傷，其餘隊伍四散。七月底，倖存者利用仍然可用的無線電設備發出通告；8月起，部分人員轉入Sierra Maestra，重建小組、取得新一批武器並保存幹部。Frank País在7月30日戰死，說明原定的多點配合已遭重創。秋天又出現針對軍方交通、供應與通信的小規模襲擊；12月2日，一支市區小組進入哈瓦那Banco Nacional de Cuba並利用廣播宣布行動，隨後帶走款項離開。各來源對Moncada及Goayería的陣亡、被俘與失聯人數採不同口徑，部分人又被重複計算，因此本文不列看似精確而無法穩定核實的傷亡總數。
dataEn: The chronology contains several verifiable landmarks. On December 2, 1952, Fidel delivered his public speech at Havana's Palacio de Deportes calling for the overthrow of the government. On April 30, 1953, the revolutionary network attacked the Goayería barracks in Havana; no weapons were carried away, and the attackers suffered severe losses. On July 26, more than a hundred armed personnel and support participants assembled before dawn and attacked Moncada at about six in the morning. They briefly controlled the barracks during the morning, but the position collapsed in the afternoon because reinforcements arrived and ammunition was insufficient. Fidel, Raúl, and others were captured or wounded, while the remaining teams scattered. Toward the end of July, survivors used still-functioning radio equipment to issue a statement. From August, some personnel entered Sierra Maestra, rebuilt small cells, obtained new supplies of weapons, and preserved the leadership cadre. Frank País was killed on July 30, demonstrating the destruction of the intended multi-point coordination. Further small attacks against military transport, supply, and communications followed during the autumn. On December 2, a small urban team entered the Banco Nacional de Cuba in Havana, announced its action by radio, and then departed with money. Sources apply different definitions to the killed, captured, and missing at Moncada and Goayería, and some people are counted more than once. For that reason, this account does not present an apparently precise total that cannot be reliably verified.
cause: 古巴革命的成因不是單一事件。1902年共和國成立後，軍隊長期作為政治裁決者；Fulgencio Batista在1933年的軍士起義中推翻Ramón Grau政府，此後又於1940年當選總統。1952年6月1日大選中，反對派票數被選舉機構作廢或重新處理，執政聯盟取得控制；Fidel雖當選眾議員，卻看不到在既有選舉制度內改變局面的可靠道路。12月2日演說因此把組織、募款、秘密訓練與奪取軍火連成一個方向，26 de Julio運動於1953年成形。Batista政府以軍隊、總統府警衛隊和特別權力打擊政治反對者，搜捕令與軍法程序使游擊隊員被捕後常難獲公開審理，這個風險直接影響後來分散、撤退與海外聯絡的安排。進攻Moncada的近因是武裝組織需要彈藥與自動武器，又認為守軍之間存在可利用的不滿、固定兵營較易奪取；但策劃者高估了部隊迅速倒戈的可能，也低估了營區防禦、援軍反應和彈藥補充速度。美國的經濟與外交影響、出口依賴和社會分配不平等提供更廣背景，卻不應被簡化成由外國直接下令。1953年7月26日是觸發大規模武裝對抗的日期，不是所有原因在該日突然出現。
causeEn: The Cuban Revolution had no single cause. After the republic was established in 1902, the army frequently acted as an arbiter of politics. Fulgencio Batista came to power through the Sergeants' Revolt of 1933, which overthrew the government of Ramón Grau, and was later elected president in 1940. In the general election of June 1, 1952, opposition votes were voided or otherwise reprocessed by the electoral authorities, allowing the governing coalition to retain control. Although Fidel was elected to Congress, he could see no reliable route to change the situation within the existing electoral system. His December 2 speech therefore connected organization, fundraising, clandestine training, and the acquisition of military weapons into a single direction, and the 26th of July Movement took shape during 1953. The Batista government used the army, the Presidential Guard, and exceptional powers against political opponents. Search warrants and military jurisdiction often prevented captured insurgents from receiving an open trial, a risk that directly affected later plans for dispersal, withdrawal, and overseas liaison. The immediate cause of the attack on Moncada was the armed organization’s need for ammunition and automatic weapons, combined with the belief that dissatisfaction among the defenders could be exploited and that a fixed barracks would be comparatively easy to seize. The planners, however, overestimated how quickly troops might defect and underestimated the barracks defense, the speed of the reinforcement response, and the difficulty of replenishing ammunition. American economic and diplomatic influence, dependence on exports, and unequal social distribution formed the broader background, but they cannot be reduced to direct orders issued from abroad. July 26, 1953, was the date that triggered large-scale armed confrontation, not the sudden appearance of every underlying cause.
impact: 影響可以分成立即、體制與長期三層。Moncada在戰術上失敗，兵營很快由政府軍重掌，Batista政權也沒有因此失去對城市的控制；但進攻者留下的武裝經驗、聯絡網與一批受傷後仍繼續活動的幹部，使政府原本以為能一次清除的組織得以延續。部分被俘者遭即決處置，Fidel與Raúl則因事件受到廣泛關注而沒有立即被處死，這使7月26日從一次失敗的襲擊變成革命運動最難抹去的公開事件。Batista利用事件擴大緊急權力、搜捕與監視，軍隊控制反而更集中；同時，山區小組避開長期占領城市，改以小隊襲擊、伏擊軍方補給線和保存幹部，證明武裝鬥爭可以由市區轉向Sierra Maestra。Raúl與Echeverría在墨西哥接續武器、人員與政治聯絡，1953年12月的市區行動也顯示即使Moncada之後，網絡仍能策動短促而有影響力的襲擊。1954年2月17日Batista離開總統位置，但他的政治影響仍大，軍方也未因此解除戒備，所以這不是革命已勝利的證明。1953年的真正效果，是迫使革命者承認固定據點攻擊的侷限，並把重心轉向可長期運作的山區游擊體系。
impactEn: The effects can be divided into immediate, institutional, and long-term levels. Moncada failed tactically: government troops recovered the barracks, and the Batista regime did not lose control of the cities. Nevertheless, the attackers preserved practical weapons experience, liaison networks, and a group of cadres who continued operating despite their wounds. The organization therefore survived an effort the government had expected to eliminate at one stroke. Some captured insurgents were summarily executed, while Fidel and Raúl, who received wide attention, were not killed immediately. As a result, July 26 became the most indelible public event in the revolutionary movement despite the military failure of the assault. Batista used the incident to expand emergency powers, arrests, and surveillance, concentrating military control still further. At the same time, mountain teams avoided prolonged occupation of urban positions and instead used small-scale attacks, ambushes against army supply routes, and the preservation of cadres to demonstrate that armed struggle could move from the cities into Sierra Maestra. Raúl and Echeverría reconnected weapons, personnel, and political contacts in Mexico, while the urban actions of December 1953 showed that the network could still organize brief but consequential attacks after Moncada. Batista left the presidency on February 17, 1954, but retained substantial political influence, and the military did not stand down. His departure therefore was not proof that the revolution had already won. The real effect of 1953 was to compel the revolutionaries to recognize the limitations of attacks on fixed strongpoints and transfer their center of gravity toward a mountain guerrilla system capable of prolonged operation.
result: 結果：若只以1953年7月26日計，Moncada主攻失敗，武器與彈藥未能帶走，城市與國家權力仍在Batista政府手中；到1953年底，這場戰役沒有推翻政府。然而，它完成了比奪取一座兵營更持久的轉折：保存了革命幹部，建立了山區根據地，使都市襲擊與鄉村游擊互相配合，並迫使運動以長期生存而非一次奪權為目標。1954年Batista下台後，軍方仍維持鎮壓，革命因而在海外集結。1956年12月6日，裝載游擊隊員的Granma由墨西哥出發，12月19日深夜至20日登陸古巴；登陸損失後，倖存者在Sierra Maestra重新建立基地，隊伍靠襲擊、伏擊、新成員加入與倒戈軍人逐漸擴大。1958年12月30日至31日的Yaguajay戰鬥及同期各地攻勢，使政府喪失對東部與中部通道的控制；1959年1月1日Batista離開古巴，數日內革命政府接管哈瓦那，武裝革命的政權更替階段至此完成。因而1953年的Moncada不是一場可以單獨宣稱勝利或失敗的終局；它是把有限的城市突擊轉化為持續六年的山區戰爭的起點，也是Fidel Castro從被俘的26 de Julio領導者轉為全國性革命領袖的轉捩點。
resultEn: Result: If the assessment is restricted to July 26, 1953, the principal attack on Moncada failed. Weapons and ammunition were not carried away, and control of the cities and national authority remained in Batista's hands. By the end of 1953, the campaign had not overthrown the government. It nevertheless produced a more durable transformation than the temporary seizure of one barracks: the revolutionary cadres were preserved, a mountain base was established, urban attacks and rural guerrilla activity were linked, and the movement was compelled to organize for long-term survival rather than a single transfer of power. After Batista left the presidency in 1954, the military continued repression, and the revolutionaries consequently concentrated their preparations abroad. On December 6, 1956, the Granma left Mexico carrying insurgents and reached Cuba during the night of December 19 to 20. Following losses during the landing, the survivors reestablished a base in Sierra Maestra. The force expanded through attacks, ambushes, new members, and army personnel who deserted. The fighting at Yaguajay from December 30 to 31, 1958, together with simultaneous advances elsewhere, deprived the government of control over major routes in the east and center of the island. Batista left Cuba on January 1, 1959, and the revolutionary government took over Havana within days, completing the regime-change phase of the armed revolution. Moncada in 1953 was therefore not a self-contained victory or defeat. It was the point at which a limited urban assault was transformed into six years of mountain warfare, and the turning point by which Fidel Castro moved from a captured leader of the 26th of July Movement to the leader of a nationwide revolution.
